summary: Quarterly business review covering usage trends, cost drivers, recent reliability incidents, and roadmap alignment. Customer is seeing increased token spend driven by new feature rollouts; evaluating tradeoffs between Hosted and Dedicated. Agreed to run benchmarks and share SOC2 + architecture docs. Action items assigned for cost breakdown, benchmarks, and infra details.
topics: Dedicated vs Hosted sizing and economics
transcript:
00:00 Sofia (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we've got about 50 minutes, agenda is usage, cost, reliability, roadmap alignment. Maya, Jordan, thanks for carving time.
00:12 Maya (Haven): Yeah thanks Sofia, appreciate it. We brought Oliver and Sam, and wanted to focus on why our token spend jumped in April.
00:20 Devon (Redwood CSM): Quick heads up, I'll share the quarter deck after, and Ravi will cover perf details later.
00:28 Oliver (Haven): Right, we launched the contextual summarization beta and that seems to be the big driver. Longer context windows, more tokens per request.
00:35 Ravi (Redwood SE): Totally, longer seq length increases cost non-linearly esp if KV cache hits are low. Are you doing prefix caching for repeated users?
00:44 Maya: We're doing some caching in app-level but not via Redwood's prefix cache yet. We assumed the platform would handle more of that, but maybe we misconfigured.
00:52 Jordan (Haven): Also noticed spikes during ETL runs, we batch analytics queries that call the model at scale.
01:00 Devon: Ok that explains both the steady higher spend and some spikes. We'll go through the cost breakdown.
01:10 Sofia: Before we dive in, any reliability incidents to note? Sam?
01:16 Sam (Haven SRE): We had two incidents in March where latency spiked ~700ms above baseline during peak; traced to autoscaler warm-up and one misrouted fallback to a higher-latency region. We logged support ticket SR-3372 and Redwood responded.
01:30 Ravi: Yeah I pulled the traces, that was a routing rule mismatch — fallback to a larger model in a different region. We've since tightened routing policies and added a transient queue to smooth autoscale.
01:42 Maya: The root cause was also our config; we had permissive model fallbacks enabled. We thought fallbacks would be same-arch but it chose a different family.
01:50 Ravi: The fallback policy will now prefer same-family quantized variants; I'll share the rule snippet after the call.
01:58 Oliver: Sounds good. Can you also confirm retention and logs? We need audit trail for a compliance review.
02:05 Devon: We'll share SOC2 docs and the audit log export link. Quick note, the docs are in the shared folder, I'll post the short links.
02:12 Maya: Great. On costs, can you walk us through the biggest drivers?
02:17 Devon: Sure — two things: average tokens per request up ~38% because of longer contexts, and request volume up ~22% from new feature launch. Also model choice: you moved from a 7B quant to a 13B variant for quality reasons which adds unit cost.
02:32 Jordan: We did that to reduce hallucinations but maybe the unit economics are worse. Is quantization an option?
02:37 Ravi: Yes — going to int8 or 4-bit quantized 13B variants can reduce GPU memory and cost. Batch execution and persistent KV caching will help too. We can run a profile to show latency/cost tradeoffs.
02:48 Maya: Can you provide expected % savings?
02:50 Ravi: Ballpark: quant + batching could shave 20-35% on token cost depending on qprofile and cache hit rate. We'll put numbers in the benchmark.
02:59 Sofia: Awesome, that will help procurement when they look at the budget. Speaking of procurement, any blockers on Dedicated?
03:06 Oliver: We're evaluating Dedicated vs staying Hosted. Dedicated gives predictability but our infra team worries about data egress and peering complexity.
03:14 Ravi: Dedicated also allows pinning model versions and deterministic latency. For egress we support VPC peering and private link, plus KMS integration for keys.
03:24 Jordan: On KMS — can Redwood integrate with our HashiCorp Vault/HSM? Our security needs HSM-backed keys for production.
03:31 Devon: Yes, we support customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations; I'll attach integration docs.
03:36 Maya: Also curious on data residency — some customers in EMEA demand that inference happen in eu-west-1. Is that available on Dedicated?
03:43 Sofia: Yes, Dedicated deployment can be in region; for Hosted we have regions but if you need full on-prem or VPC Private deployment we can do private plane.
03:52 Oliver: We might need on-prem for a specific regulated client, but that's a longer discussion. For this quarter, optimizing costs is priority.
04:00 Ravi: Ok, technical plan: we'll run a benchmark with your real workload sample — 50k requests across typical session lengths. We'll compare current 13B hosted variant, a quantized 13B, and a 7B + reranker flow. We'll measure latency P50/P95 and tokens per dollar.
04:18 Maya: Timeline?
04:19 Ravi: I can run initial bench by 2026-05-28 if you send the workload sample and credentials for a test tenant.
04:27 Maya: We'll get that to you — Jordan will share the sample and peak windows.
04:31 Jordan: Yep, I'll send the sample by EOD Tuesday.
04:34 Devon: I'll send the cost deck and recommend batching, cache TTLs, and a suggested quant profile.
04:40 Sofia: On reliability, Ravi mentioned routing. Are there guardrails we can add to avoid cross-family fallbacks?
04:45 Ravi: We'll add stricter policy rules and an alert when fallback occurs more than X times per minute. Also propose a canary policy for model rollouts.
04:55 Maya: That alerting is key; we missed the March spike until customers complained.
04:59 Ravi: We'll set up a per-route latency SLO alert and token consumption spike alert, and tie it to Slack channel ops.
05:08 Oliver: What's the expected impact on latency if we enable batching more aggressively? Some of our use cases are interactive.
05:15 Ravi: Aggressive batching reduces cost but adds per-request latency. With dynamic batching we can maintain P50 sub-200ms and bring cost down; P95 may increase modestly. We'll quantify this in the benchmark.
05:28 Maya: Any limitations with our current network? Jordan, any egress charges we should worry about?
05:33 Jordan: We saw some network egress cost in April due to heavier logging exports. We can look at retention policies to cut that.
05:40 Devon: Good point — audit log retention and trace sampling are levers for cost too. We'll recommend retention settings.
05:47 Sofia: Let's talk roadmap alignment — upcoming Redwood features that matter to you?
05:52 Maya: Persistent KV cache and a better model catalog filter are top asks. If caching reduces tokens, that's A huge win.
05:59 Ravi: Persistent KV cache is in our prioritized roadmap for Q3; we'll share the RFC link. It should materially improve repeated context workloads.
06:06 Oliver: Also a per-route cost dashboard for product owners would help convince leadership.
06:11 Devon: We already have token-level cost breakdown in Console; I'll send a screenshot and link to set up product-level dashboards.
06:18 Maya: Okay. On security docs, can you share SOC2 and the architecture diagram? We need to feed to internal auditors by next Thursday.
06:25 Devon: Yes — SOC2 cert and architecture whitepaper link coming after the call.
06:30 Sofia: Anything else before recap?
06:32 Sam: Quick note — retention of model inputs for debug, can we mask PII automatically? We need guidance.
06:39 Ravi: We have redaction tooling and optional automatic PII scrubbers at ingest; I'll share config examples.
06:45 Maya: Perfect.
06:46 Sofia: Recap: Devon to send cost breakdown and SOC2/docs; Ravi to run benchmark (due 2026-05-28); Jordan to share workload sample (due 2026-05-25); propose Dedicated sizing by 2026-06-05. I'll schedule the perf deep dive.
07:03 Oliver: Thanks everyone.
07:06 Speaker 1: (crosstalk) and then we'll loop in procurement.
07:10 Sofia: Thanks, meeting adjourned.

Note: transcription imperfect in places; some proper nouns and acronyms may be misrecognized (e.g., KV cache, V P C, SOC2 as SOC two). Links to docs will be shared via email/slack after call: https://redwood.ai/docs/soc2, https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/2026/q2, shared deck: https://redwood.ai/sales/decks/haven-qbr-2026-05-22.pdf
